_comment: SkillBench task set v2 — every brief carries verifiable ground truth: numbers that must reconcile, constraints that must be honoured, names that must appear. checks[] are deterministic regexes the harness scores alongside the judge (see REPORT.md §6 for why v2 exists). Frozen once the first official v2 run publishes.

tasks.input:
Rank these for next quarter using RICE and show your work:
1. Onboarding redesign — reach 4000 users/qtr, impact 2, confidence 0.8, effort 2 person-months.
2. SSO — reach 500 accounts, impact 3, confidence 1.0, effort 3.
3. Dark mode — reach 8000, impact 0.5, confidence 0.9, effort 1.

checks.why: computes dark mode's RICE score correctly

tasks.input: PRD for an in-app referral program. Hard constraints: must ship by November 15, iOS app only for v1 (web later), and we have exactly 2 engineers. Goal: +15% signups in Q4. Existing users invite colleagues; both sides get a credit.

Draft the quarterly board update from these facts, and only these: ARR $3.6M (was $3.0M last quarter), monthly burn $250k, cash $3.5M, team of 24 (hired 3), churn steady at 2% monthly, enterprise pilot with 2 logos started. Don't invent numbers we didn't give you.

Customer-facing incident update, mid-incident: EU region degraded since 09:12 UTC (API errors ~20%), cause identified as a failed cache-cluster upgrade, fix deploying now, ETA full restore 11:00 UTC. US/APAC unaffected. Second update of the incident.

Blameless postmortem from this timeline: 14:02 config change deployed to payment router; 14:19 error-rate alert fires (checkout failures 12%); 14:31 on-call pages platform team; 14:47 config rolled back; 14:52 recovery confirmed. ~9,400 failed checkouts. The config change skipped canary because it was marked 'low risk'.

checks.why: identifies the config change as the trigger

tasks.input: Plan the migration of our 2TB Postgres 12 primary to Postgres 16 with near-zero downtime — writes must keep flowing. We'll gate the cutover behind the feature flag pg16_cutover. Include the rollback path and what we verify before flipping.

We started the quarter with 2,400 paying customers and 168 cancelled during it. 61 of the 168 cited pricing; 44 cited a missing integration; the rest gave no reason. Compute the churn rate and tell me what to do first, with the math shown.
Write the readout: control converted 4.0% (400 of 10,000), variant 4.6% (460 of 10,000). Product wants to ship it today. Give the lift, whether this is statistically solid, and the recommendation.

checks.why: computes the lift correctly (15% relative / 0.6pp absolute)

tasks.input: Competitive teardown for our meeting-notes product against the three competitors we actually lose to: Voxel (bottom-up freemium, loved UX), Brightline (enterprise, SOC2 + SSO everywhere), and Cascade (cheapest, aggressive on price). Cover each and where we win.
Our unit cost is $18/seat/month (infra + support). Finance requires 70% gross margin minimum. Competitors charge $49-$79. Recommend the price point and defend it — show the margin math.

Q3 OKRs for a 6-person support team. Current: CSAT 78%, first-response time 9 hours, backlog 340 tickets. Leadership wants CSAT at 90% and first response under 4 hours by end of quarter. Make them real OKRs, not a task list.

checks.why: grounds in at least one baseline number

tasks.input: Draft performance feedback for a mid-level engineer. Facts: missed the partner-API deadline in May (slipped 3 weeks, told nobody until the standup before); led the June 3 incident response excellently (praised by two teams); code review turnaround consistently under a day. Balanced, specific, actionable.

One-page summary for the CEO from these numbers only: cash $1.8M, burn $300k/mo, pipeline $2.2M weighted, two enterprise deals ($400k, $250k ACV) at contract stage, hiring freeze in effect. What's our runway and what are the decision points? Do not invent figures.
